31-2530210000.title: Driver Safety Instructor
31-2530210000.description:
Occupational Description


Driving instructors teach students between the ages of 14 to 18 motor vehicle laws, vehicle operating tasks, occupant protection, establishing vehicle position, limited space movements, human functions, traffic flow tasks, driving environment, factors affecting performance (risk, attitude, emotion), other roadway users, alcohol and other drugs, insurance, responses to vehicle failure and driver errors, car control and mixing with traffic, and response to traffic conditions during the minimum of 20 hours of classroom instruction. The instructor teaches and observes students’ driving during the required five hours of behind-the-wheel training. Once a student has passed a written and driving examination, the instructor enters this information into the Driver Licnesing waiver system and sends it electronically to the DMV. The student can then either apply online or in-person at a driver’s license office, so a Provisional Operator’s Permit or School Permit can be issued.

Licensure Requirements


Applicants must: 1. Be at least 21 years of age; 2. Have held a valid driver’s license from their state of residence for a period of at least two consecutive years immediately preceding the date of application; 3. Have a high school diploma or its equivalent; 4. Possess competence as outlined in a driver’s education endorsement or the equiva…
31-2530210000.agency: Nebraska Dept. of Motor Vehicles · Driver Licensing Services

00-28.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary - OTI
00-28.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI) - Ocean Freight Forwarder requires that the designated employee for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. Details can be found at the FMC web sites http://www.fmc.gov/cfr/515.htm, http://www.fmc.gov/Help/OTI.htm, and the Code of Federal Regulations (46CFR515) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr515_02.html.
00-28.agency: Federal Maritime Commission · Bureau of Tariffs, Certification and Licensing

00-29.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary -NVOCC
00-29.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI)- Non-Vessel-Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) requires that the qualifying individual for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. Details can be found at the FMC web sites: http://www.fmc.gov/cfr/515.htm, http://www.fmc.gov/Help/OTI.htm, and the Code of Federal Regulations (46CFR515) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr515_02.html.
00-29.agency: Federal Maritime Commission · Bureau of Tariffs, Certification and Licensing

00-67.title: Barge Supervisor
00-67.description: A Barge Supervisor is required to pass an exam, have 3 years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology, plus at least 168 days of related experience. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-67.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-37.title: Chief Mate - Upper Level
00-37.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Mate - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on Any Gross Tons oceangoing steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Second Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-37.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-34.title: Deck Officers
00-34.description: The navigation of a vessel and management of the deck department is the responsibility of the Deck Officers. Deck officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Master, Chief Mate, Second Mate, Third Mate, Mate and Operator), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam, Motor, Sail or Auxiliary Sail), vessel tonnage (from not more than 5 to any gross register tons), and route (e.g., Inland, Great Lakes, Near Coastal or Oceans). Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-34.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-40.title: Master - Lower Level
00-40.description: Obtaining a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Lower Level requires a specified amount of qualifying service based on details such as vessel size and area of operation (ocean, near coastal, Great Lakes, or inland). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-40.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-36.title: Master - Upper Level
00-36.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Chief Mate on ocean Any Gross Tons steam or motor vessels; or 180 days as Chief Mate plus 360 days as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-36.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-66.title: Offshore Installation Manager - OIM
00-66.description: An Offshore Installation Manager (OIM) requires passing an exam and four years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 168 days of related work experience. Specialized training in rig stability, oil well control or operation, firefighting and survival at sea are required. OIMs apply for an OIM Unrestricted License or one of four specialized licenses: OIM Surface Units on Location, OIM Surface Units Underway, OIM Bottom Bearing Units Underway, and OIM Bottom-Bearing Units on Location. Federal regulations can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SECTION=470&YEAR=1999&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-66.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-44.title: Pilot (Ship)
00-44.description: A license or endorsement as a Pilot is route-specific and requires experience navigating the body of water specified. A written exam and physical exam are also required. Further information on Pilot requirements can be found on the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2002-title46-vol1/CFR-2002-title46-vol1-part10.
00-44.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-69.title: Radar Observer
00-69.description: The Radar Observer certificate is issued by the United States Coast Guard to licensed deck officers. It requires specialized training and examination in radar navigation and is issued for 5 years. Further information can be found in the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10.305) at web site http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50176913269+4+2+0&WAISaction=retrieve and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-69.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-39.title: Third Mate - Upper Level
00-39.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Mate - Upper Level requires 1080 days service in the deck department of ocean steam or motor vessels with 6 months as Able Seaman (AB); or graduate from an approved marine academy; or completion of an approved 3 year apprentice mate training program; or 360 days as Master on ocean steam or motor vessels greater than 200 GT while licensed as a Master 1600 Gross Tons. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-39.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-68.title: Ballast Control Operator
00-68.description: A United States Coast Guard Ballast Control Operator is required to pass an exam and to have 1 year related experience, including at least 28 days as a trainee under a licensed Ballast Control Operator or a degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 28 days as a trainee. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://frwebgate2.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=051618583+1+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve, http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-68.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-46.title: Chief Engineer
00-46.description: To be licensed by the United States Coast Guard as a Chief Engineer, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer; or while holding a First Assistant Engineer license, complete 360 days of service as follows: a minimum of 180 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer plus a minimum of 360 days as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer, Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-46.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-51.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal)
00-51.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal) include 1,440 days at sea, with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer & 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-51.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-50.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-50.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans), include 1,800 days at sea, with 720 days as a Licensed Engineer & 900 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-50.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-53.title: Designated Duty Engineer
00-53.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Designated Duty Engineer include specified service time at sea, with experience as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED) on a vessel of specified horsepower. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-53.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-45.title: Engineering Officers
00-45.description: The propulsion plant of a vessel and management of the engineering department is the responsibility of the Engineering Officers. Engineering officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Chief Engineer, First Assistant Engineer, Second Assistant Engineer, Third Assistant Engineer, Assistant Engineer and Designated Duty Engineer), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam or Motor), horsepower (from 1,000 to any horsepower), and route (e.g., Near Coastal or Oceans). License limitations for deck and engineering officers, including tonnage and horsepower, are based on the type of experience of each applicant and the passing of applicable written examinations. Each license has separate general, service and examination requirements. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-45.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

31-2911270000.title: Speech-language Pathologist
31-2911270000.description:
Occupational Description


Speech-Language Pathologists apply principles and methods associated with the development and disorders of human communication skills and dysphagia. These principles and methods include screening, assessment, evaluation, treatment, prevention, consultation, and restorative modalities for speech, voice, language, language-based learning, hearing, swallowing, or other upper aerodigestive functions, for the purpose of improving quality of life by reducing impairments of body functions and structures, activity limitations, participation restrictions, and environmental barriers. Practice of speech-language pathology does not include the practice of medical diagnosis, medical treatment, or surgery.

Licensure Requirements


Applicants must: 1. Meet one of the following: A. Have a master’s degree or its equivalent in speech-language pathology from an academic program accredited by the Education Standards Board of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association; -OR- B. For applicants who graduated prior to September 1, 2007, present proof of a master’s degree, doctoral degree, or the equivalent of a master’s degree or doctoral degree in audiology from an academic program; -OR- C. For applicants who graduated on or after September 1, 2007, present proof of a doctoral degree or its equivalent in audiology; accredited by the Education St…
31-2911270000.agency: Nebraska Dept. of Health & Human Services · Public Health Division, Licensure Unit, Office of Rehabilitation & Community Services · Public Health Division, Licensure Unit, Office of Rehabilitation & Community Services

31-3920110000.title: Race Horse Stable Attendant (Groom)
31-3920110000.description:
Occupational Description


Grooms are employed by licensed Trainers at a racetrack. They are responsible for the care of the horse and barn area, including the feeding, bathing, and maintaining the general appearance of the horse.

Licensure Requirements


A groom must be at least 16 years old.A felony conviction may be grounds for denial.

Fees


License Fee - $15.00.

Renewal


Renewal is required annually by December 31. The renewal fee is $15.00.Fingerprints are required every 5 years.

31-3930190000.title: Race Track Worker
31-3930190000.description:
Occupational Description


The NE Racing & Gaming Commission issues licenses for a variety of racing-related occupations. These employees work for the racetracks, and must meet individual track restrictions. License are typically issued after an applicant has secured employment at a racetrack.

Licensure Requirements


Individuals working at racetracks in Nebraska must be at least 16 years of age. A felony conviction may be grounds for denial of a license. Applications must be completed and signed by management before submission.

Fees


License Fees will vary based on the specific job performed, with most costing between $15.00 - $50.00.

Renewal


Renewal is required annually by December 31. The renewal fee varies based on the specific job performed, with most costing between $15.00 - $50.00.Fingerprints are required every 5 years.

31-1710220000.title: Land Surveyor, Registered
31-1710220000.description:
Occupational Description


Land Surveyors measure the distance, direction, and angle between two points and the elevation of points, lines, and contours on the earth’s surface. They research legal records and look for evidence of previous boundaries.Surveyors plan the fieldwork, select survey reference points, and determine the precise location ofany natural or constructed features in the survey project area.The surveyor will record the results of the survey and verify the accuracy of the data in addition topreparation of plats, maps, charts, and reports for legal documentation.

Licensure Requirements


The applicant must have at least six years of surveying experience, of which at least three must have been in a responsible position.Credit may be given for education that has been approved by the Board.

Fees


Application Fee- $40.00Registration Fee- $100.00

Renewal


Renewal is required biennially. The renewal fee is $100.00.Completion of 30 hours of professional development is required to qualify for renewal.
31-1710220000.agency: Nebraska Board of Examiners for Land Surveyors

31-1310110000.title: Athlete Agent
31-1310110000.description:
Occupational Description


Athlete Agent is defined as an individual who enters into an agency contract with a student-athlete or, directly or indirectly, recruits a student-athlete to enter into an agency contract

Licensure Requirements


They must complete the required forms provided by our office.

Fees


Initial License Fee - $300.00Reciprocal License Fee - $150.00

Renewal


Required to renew every 2 years. Renewal fee is $150.00
31-1310110000.agency: Nebraska Secretary of State · Licensing Division

31-2720210002.title: Mixed Martial Artist
31-2720210002.description:
Occupational Description


A Mixed Martial Artist is any athlete that competes in professional martial arts events in Nebraska.

Licensure Requirements


All Mixed Martial Artists must pass a physical examination before being allowed to compete in a sporting event. Mixed Martial Artists must be in training for a minimum of 30 days prior to being issued a license and approved to compete in a mixed martial arts match. No contestant under the age of 18 years shall be permitted in a professional mixed martial arts match without written parent/guardian permission.

Fees


License Fee- $20.00 (Payable at first event)

Renewal


All licenses expire on June 30 following the date of issuance.

00-64.title: Enrolled Agent - EA
00-64.description: Requirements to become an enrolled agent of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) are one of the following (1) pass an exam; or (2) document 5 years of relevant experience as an employee for the IRS. Continuing professional education hours every three-year cycle is required for renewal of the credential. Further information can be found at the IRS web site: http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/agents/index.html.
00-64.agency: Internal Revenue Service · Enrolled Practitioner Program Unit

31-2520210000.title: Elementary School Teacher
31-2520210000.description:
Occupational Description


An Elementary School Teacher teaches pupils in public or private elementary schools basic academic, social, and other formative skills.

Licensure Requirements


See ‘Teacher’

Fees


See ‘Teacher’

Renewal


See ‘Teacher’
31-2520210000.agency: Nebraska Dept. of Education · Educator Certification

31-2320930000.title: Abstracter, Registered
31-2320930000.description:
Occupational Description


A Registered Abstracter is an individual, registered under the Abstracters Act, holding an operative certificate of registration, who for a fee or other valuable consideration, compiles and certifies Abstracts of Title or prepares Reports of Title for real property in any county within the state of Nebraska.

Licensure Requirements


Any individual desiring to become a registered abstracter shall file an application for registration with the board. Such applicant shall have reached the age of majority, shall not have been convicted of a felony. Each applicant for registration shall take the written examination prescribed by section 76-543. The board shall prescribe a written examination to determine the proficiency of the applicant. If the applicant passes the examination and meets the other requirements of section 76-542, the board shall issue a certificate of registration designating him or her to be a registered abstracter.

Fees


Registered Abstracters – Application Fee $ 50.00 Examination Fee $ 75.00 Re-Examination Fee $ 75.00 Certificate of Registration $ 200.00 Transfer Certificate of Registration $ 10.00 (To New Employer) Duplicate Certificate of Registration Fee $ 50.00 (Additional Company) Certificate of Authority – Application Fee $ 100.00 Certificate of Authority $ 400.00

Renewal


Every tw…

00-79.title: Aircraft Dispatcher
00-79.description: An Aircraft Dispatcher certificate requires that the individual has work experience as an aircraft dispatcher or related occupation such as pilot. Training in aircraft dispatching and passing written and practical tests are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.51-65.70, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ

31-5330320001.title: Truck Driver (Heavy)
31-5330320001.description:
Occupational Description


Truck Drivers operate a variety of trucks to transport materials and finished products from one location to another location. Heavy Truck Drivers drive a single-body truck which carries materials weighing three tons or more. There are a variety of heavy-duty trucks, including dump trucks, tow trucks, flatbed trucks, redi-mix trucks, and tank trucks. (NOTE: In Nebraska, Truck Driver Heavy and Light or Delivery are combined under one license.)

Licensure Requirements


Commercial Drivers Licenses (CDLs) are required for individuals driving a vehicle that weighs more than 26,000 pounds (gross vehicle weight rating), carries 16 or more passengers, or transports placarded amounts of hazardous materials. Applicants for CDL Intrastate (within Nebraska) Classes “A,”“B,” or “C” must be 18 years of age.Interstate drivers (across state lines) Class “A”, “B,” or “C” must be 21 years of age. All individuals holding a Nebraska Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) are required to certify tothe DMV what type of operation they engage in. There are four categories:. Category A - Interstate & Non-Excepted;. Category B - Interstate & Excepted;. Category C - Intrastate & Non-Excepted;. Category D - Intrastate & Excepted.In addition, if they operate in Category A (Interstate & Non-Excepted), Drivers are required to provide the DMV with a current copy of…
31-5330320001.agency: Nebraska Dept. of Motor Vehicles · Driver Licensing Services

31-2920560000.title: Veterinary Technician
31-2920560000.description:
Occupational Description


Veterinary Technicians work under the supervision of Veterinarians. They may be responsible for tasks such as conducting medical tests in a laboratory environment for use in the treatment and diagnosis of diseases in animals; preparing vaccines and serums for prevention of diseases; preparing tissue samples, taking blood samples, and executing laboratory tests, such as urinalysis and blood counts; cleaning and sterilizing instruments and materials; maintaining equipment and machines; and assisting veterinarians during surgical procedures.

Licensure Requirements


Applicants must: 1. Pass the Veterinary Technician National Examination; 2. Be a graduate of an AVMA-accredited Veterinary Technician School or program. 3. Be at least 19 years of age; 4. Possess good moral character A temporary license may be granted for no more than one year to a person who has graduated from an AVMA-accredited Veterinary Technician School or program, pending the results of a passing score on the Veterinary Technician Examination (VTNE). If an applicant has completed education, training, or service that they believe is substantially similar to the education required for this credential while they were a member of the armed forces of the United States, active or reserve, the National Guard of any state, the military reserves of any state, or the naval…
31-2920560000.agency: Nebraska Dept. of Health & Human Services · Public Health Licensure Unit

31-2911310000.title: Veterinarian
31-2911310000.description:
Occupational Description


A Veterinarian is a person who has received a doctorate in veterinary medicine from an accredited school of veterinary medicine or its equivalent. A Veterinarian can practice veterinary surgery, obstetrics, dentistry, and all other branches or specialties of veterinary medicine.

Licensure Requirements


Licensure in veterinary medicine and surgery may be obtained either by: Examination- Applicants must have passed the North American Veterinary Licensing Examination (NAVLE) within the last five years with a converted score of at least 70; -OR- Reciprocity- Applicants must meet both of the following conditions: 1. Have been actively engaged in the practice of veterinary medicine and surgery at least one of the three years immediately preceding the application under a license in another state or territory of the United States, the District of Columbia, or a Canadian province; 2. Have passed either the NAVLE or NBE/CCT with a converted score of at least 70. All applicants are also required to complete a Nebraska State Jurisprudence Examination, and to pass a fingerprint criminal background check. If the applicant is going to administer, prescribe, or dispense controlled substances, he or she will need to provide proof of his or her federal DEA registration. If an applicant has completed education, training, or service that they bel…
31-2911310000.agency: Nebraska Dept. of Health & Human Services · Public Health Licensure Unit

31-5180310000.title: Wastewater Treatment Operator, Certified
31-5180310000.description:
Occupational Description


A Certified Wastewater Treatment Operator is an individual who is responsible for process controldecisions at a municipal or industrial wastewater treatment facility.

Licensure Requirements


Applicants must:1. Have one to four years of combined education and experience, depending upon level ofcertification.2. Pass a written examination for initial certification, which lasts for two years.

Fees


Application for Certification & Examination- $150.00Application for Retest- $125.00Application for Certification by Reciprocity- $150.00Application for One-Year Temporary Certification- $125.00

Renewal


Renewal is required biennially.Completion of at least 2 CEU’s (20 contact hours) of approvedcontinuing education during each 2-year certificationcycle is required to qualify for renewal.

31-1940910001.title: Wastewater Treatment Professional, Onsite Certified
31-1940910001.description:
Occupational Description


A Certified Onsite Wastewater Treatment Professional is an individual who is certified as an installer,inspector, soil evaluator, or pumper to perform work on an onsite wastewater treatment facility.

Licensure Requirements


Applicants must pass a written examination for initial certification, which lasts for 2 years

Fees


Exam Fee- $50.00Certification by Examination for Journeyman Installer or Journeyman Pumper- $100.00Certification by Examination for Master Installer, MasterPumper, Soil Evaluator, or Inspector- $300.00

Renewal


Renewal is required biennially at the end of every odd-numberedyear.The renewal fee for Journeyman Installer or JourneymanPumper Certification is $100.00.The renewal fee for Master Installer, Master Pumper, SoilEvaluator, or Inspector Certification is $300.00.Completion of at least 12 PDH’s (Professional DevelopmentHours) of approved continuing education during each2-year certification cycle is required to qualify for renewal.

Occupational Description


Water Well Drilling Contractor- A principal officer, director, manager, or owner-operator of any business engaged in the construction or decommissioning of water wells. Water Well Contractor does NOT include: An individual who constructs a water well, or who decommissions a driven sandpoint well, which is on land owned by him or her and used by him or her for farming, ranching, or agricultural purposes, or as his or her place of abode; A water well drilling supervisor. Water Well Drilling Supervisor- Any individual engaged in the construction or decommissioning of water wells. Such supervisor may have discretionary and supervisory authority over other employees of a water well contractor. Water Well Drilling Supervisor does NOT include: An individual who constructs a water well, or decommissions a driven sandpoint well, which is on land owned by him or her and used by him or her for farming, ranching, or agricultural purposes, or as his or her place of abode; Any licensed water well contractor. Water Well Monitoring Technician- Any individual engaged solely in the measuring of ground water levels, the collection of ground water samples from existing water wells, or the inspection of installed water well equipment or pumping systems.
